claims.location: scope: rows 1-40 (20 HF*.raw files x 2 SILAC channels)
claims.value: cell arm only; 18 QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_1..18 tissue runs excluded (blocked)
claims.evidence: The 20 HF* raw files are exactly the 20 raw files in txt_cells.zip summary.txt (human GBM TIC cultures treated with LSD1i or DMSO). The 18 QEPLus tissue runs (EpiProfile 2.0, SILAC mode, LightR/HeavyR) carry only numbers 1-18; no deposited file, protocol or the available paper text maps them to normal vs tumour tissue, vehicle vs LSD1i, or mouse. Fig. 1E legend gives only group sizes ("normal (filled circles) and tumor (empty circles) tissues ... vehicle (n = 12) or LSD1i (n = 6)"). Excluded: QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_1.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_2.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_3.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_4.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_5.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_6.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_7.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_8.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_9.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_10.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_11.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_12.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_13.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_14.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_15.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_16.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_17.raw, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_18.raw. Listed in annotations/BLOCKED.md.

claims.value: SILAC light (GBM TIC histones) / SILAC heavy (histone super-SILAC internal standard)
claims.evidence: summary.txt: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty, Labels1 Arg10 for all 20 files (rule 14). Protocol: sample histones "mixed with an approximately equal amount of a heavy-labelled histone super-SILAC mix ... internal standard". Paper Fig. 1E legend: "L is the sample and H is the internal standard". Data check (rule 6): median L/H of H3K4me2 peptide TK(di)QTAR rises with LSD1i, as the paper reports (605051 DMSO 1.32 -> LSD1i 2.18; 700142 p34 DMSO 3.16 -> LSD1i 5.03; BT165 LSD1i 10.1), consistent with light = study sample.

claims.value: GBM TIC <ID> <DMSO|LSD1i> [<passage>] <MS batch> glio_<n> (light); histone super-SILAC mix aliquot in <run> (heavy)
claims.evidence: Each raw file name carries MS batch (HF170509/HF180122/HF180412/HF180607), run number, TIC culture ID (605051, BT165, 700142, 906080, 606012), treatment (DMSO / LSD1i) and for some a passage (p15/p24/p34/p41); MaxQuant Experiment names repeat them. Each light source = one histone preparation from one culture/treatment. The 20 heavy source names are aliquots of ONE physical pool (the histone super-SILAC mix), one name per run as required by validation.md:22-23 / sdrf-tools build.

claims.value: 1..10 within DMSO and within DDP_38003 (light); pooled (heavy)
claims.evidence: Rule 3 / README.adoc:330: numbering restarts per factor value. Each of the 10 DMSO and 10 LSD1i samples is an independent culture preparation (different TIC, MS batch or passage), so each gets its own number; the DMSO and LSD1i halves of the same batch/TIC/passage pair share a number: 1=605051 HF170509, 2=BT165 HF170509, 3=BT165 HF180122, 4=700142 HF180412 p24, 5=700142 HF180412 p34, 6=906080 HF180412, 7=700142 HF180607, 8=906080 HF180607, 9=606012 HF180607 p41, 10=606012 HF180607 p15.

claims.value: Homo sapiens; brain; glioblastoma; cell; cell type not available
claims.evidence: Paper: "human patient-derived GBM TICs" grown as spheroids from human GBM specimens. TICs are primary patient-derived cultures, not Cellosaurus cell lines (BT165 has no Cellosaurus entry; sdrf-tools cellline returned an unrelated fuzzy hit BT-16), so the cell-lines template is not declared and material type = cell. No CL term for "tumor-initiating cell" is stated -> cell type not available.

claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[pooled sample], characteristics[sample type], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[disease], characteristics[material type] rows 1-40 (heavy rows; light rows: sample type study sample, pooled sample not pooled)
claims.value: Homo sapiens; pooled; reference; other fields not available
claims.evidence: Protocol: "heavy-labelled histone super-SILAC mix, used as internal standard". Its composition is not stated for this deposit (Supplementary Materials inaccessible), so no SN= list. Organism Homo sapiens: the same labs analysed GBM histones against a super-SILAC mix of Arg10-labelled human breast cancer cell lines (Noberini 2018, PMC5934616: MDA-MB-231, MDA-MB-468, MDA-MB-453, MDA-MB-361 ...), and only the human histone FASTA was searched.
Per-patient demographics are only in table S2 (Supplementary Materials, HTTP 403); not inferred.
All 20 HF* raw headers contain "Q Exactive HF - Orbitrap MS"; the 18 excluded QEPLus runs are Q Exactive Plus.

Protocol: histones chemically acylated with D6-acetic anhydride, then "in-gel digested with trypsin". Because lysines are blocked, cleavage is effectively Arg-C-like and MaxQuant used Enzyme ArgC (summary.txt) - recorded as the search rule; the SDRF carries the digestion enzyme (batch rule 2).

limitations: PARTIAL SCOPE: 18 of 38 raw files (mouse-xenograft brain tissue arm, QEPLus_210305_RN_glio_1..18, PRO-PIC + EpiProfile 2.0, SILAC internal standard) are not annotated: no run -> sample (normal/tumour, vehicle/LSD1i, mouse) map is deposited or in the accessible paper text. Listed in BLOCKED.md.

Supplementary Materials of the Sci Transl Med paper (MS methods, table S2 with TIC patient data, dose/duration of the histone experiment) returned HTTP 403 at science.org and were not bypassed; only the author postprint main text was read.
TIC IDs (605051, BT165, 700142, 906080, 606012) cannot be mapped to the paper GBM#n names; the paper reports fig. S2A for 4 TICs (GBM#22, #11, #10, #18) while the deposit holds 5 IDs.

Super-SILAC mix composition not stated for this deposit: pooled sample = pooled without SN= list; organism Homo sapiens inferred from the labs' published histone super-SILAC mixes (Noberini 2018) and the human-only search database.

Precursor mass tolerance 6 ppm taken from the PRIDE protocol text, which also states an outdated MaxQuant version and a fragment tolerance contradicted by parameters.txt (20 ppm). MaxQuant main-search tolerance not deposited.
Biological-replicate pairing (DMSO and LSD1i of the same batch/TIC/passage sharing a number) is inferred from file names; whether those halves come from one split culture is not stated.
MaxQuant raw-file names use spaces where the deposited files use underscores (e.g. "HF170509_RN_glio_7 605051 DMSO" = HF170509_RN_glio_7_605051_DMSO.raw); mapping is one-to-one.
Cleavage agent recorded as Trypsin (digestion enzyme, batch rule 2); MaxQuant searched with the ArgC rule because lysines were D3-acetylated before digestion.
techsdrf not installed: instrument and scan range read from HTTP-range raw headers with a regex script (scripts/rawhead2.py).
